title: A type VI secretion ADP-ribosyltransferase Rhs toxin selectively modifies charged tRNAThr(GGU) anticodon loops to block ACC codon decoding.
data_url: https://europepmc.org/api/fulltextRepo?pprId=PMC13617354 (supplementary zip; contains only gkag922_supplemental_file.pdf plus figure images)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the Europe PMC supplementary archive (3.88 MB): 12 figure images plus one 11-page PDF. Extracted the PDF text page by page: every page is a figure legend (AlphaFold3 confidence plots, gel photographs) plus two DNA template sequences on page 9. No table, no CSV/TSV/XLSX, no numeric data file anywhere. Grepped the full open-access text for accessions, deposits and repository names: the only identifiers are PDB 8S2M and 5ZJ5, which the text names as DALI structure-comparison hits (other labs' structures), not depositions.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biological findings themselves (TreThr is an ADP-ribosyltransferase that modifies the GGU anticodon of charged thrT/thrV tRNAs and blocks ACC decoding) come from reading the paper; the underlying gels and assays exist only as images.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified in the files. There is no dataset. The data availability statement says data are 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material', and that supplement is an 11-page PDF of figure legends and gel photographs. No repository deposit (no GEO, SRA, PRIDE, Zenodo, Dryad or PDB entry of their own); the two PDB IDs in the text are cited comparison structures.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. Nothing is in a column anywhere. The implicit label (which tRNA isoacceptor a toxin modifies) would have to be read off gel images in a PDF and then constructed by hand for this single toxin.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL as a dataset, though sequences are obtainable. The paper gives one toxin domain (RhsF residues 1393-1513) and two DNA reporter templates as text; everything else would be fetched from UniProt/GenBank from scratch.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL. All quantitative readouts are gel band intensities and growth-spot dilutions shown as images; no numeric values with units are tabulated.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, and this is the decisive one. The unit of observation is one toxin-immunity pair from one species (Chromobacterium violaceum), with a handful of mutants and four threonine tRNA isoacceptors tested. One row, against a ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, but only because there is nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts to compare; the supplement matches the figure list in the text exactly (S1-S10).

a8_label_provenance.note: The biology is measured, not predicted: biotin-NAD labelling and acid-urea gels. But note the paper's structures are AlphaFold3 models, so any structure-based feature here would be a model output, not an experiment.

existing_models.name: ARTNet, a deep-learning predictor of bacterial ADP-ribosyltransferase toxins (Bioinformatics, 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; abstract states it predicts ADP-ribosyltransferase toxins from bacterial genomes using domain subsequences plus data augmentation to cope with few training examples.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Target specificity: the search result quotes that each ADP-ribosyltransferase modifies a specific residue of its substrate and the mechanism of that specificity is poorly understood. That is exactly the gap this paper fills for one toxin, by hand.

existing_models.name: Bastion6, a support-vector-machine predictor of type VI secretion system effectors (Bioinformatics, 2018)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported accuracy 0.943 and area under the curve 0.976 on its own curated split; a 2025 bioRxiv convolutional-network successor using protein language model features reports improvements.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural backbone for toxin sequences, and RNA-FM for tRNA, but there is no label table to attach a head to.

integration.partner_dataset: SecReT6 (a database of bacterial type VI secretion systems) could supply thousands of effector sequences, but this paper contributes one labelled example to it.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this paper alone: one measured toxin-substrate pair is an anecdote, not a training signal.

controls.positive_control: None available: no held-out measurements exist.
controls.negative_control: Not runnable; there is no model to ablate.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be trained from this paper; it establishes, for a single Chromobacterium violaceum toxin, that ADP-ribosylation targets the GGU anticodon of charged threonine tRNAs.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a bacterial toxin's protein sequence to predict which transfer RNA it chemically modifies.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on toxin protein sequences paired with their confirmed RNA or protein targets. This paper supplies exactly one such pair, so the examples would have to be assembled from dozens of separate papers.
plain_idea.predict: Which transfer RNA isoacceptor (the specific tRNA species carrying a given anticodon) a toxin attacks. Ground truth here came from biotin-tagged NAD labelling followed by gel electrophoresis, read off images.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Microbiologists studying bacterial warfare would use it to guess a new toxin's target before doing the assay, which currently takes months. But the idea needs a multi-paper curation effort, not this paper.

more_or_better_data.why: One toxin-substrate pair from one species, versus ARTNet's genome-scale training set of ADP-ribosyltransferase toxins and Bastion6's curated effector set.

confidence_score.why: No replicate numeric measurements are tabulated anywhere; all readouts are gel images, so no noise estimate is possible.

models_beatable.why: Not a meaningful question here: with one labelled example there is nothing to beat them with. ARTNet (2024) is recent and Bastion6 (2018) is old but both were trained on hundreds to thousands of sequences.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: there is no feature/label table in this paper to train on, so the existing model cannot be used as our baseline on our data.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The only machine-learning project in the area - predicting a bacterial toxin's RNA or protein substrate from its sequence - would need a curated table of toxin-target pairs built from many publications, to which this paper adds a single row. Partly served already by ARTNet (ADP-ribosyltransferase toxin detection) and Bastion6 (type VI secretion effector detection), neither of which predicts the specific substrate.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no feature or label table to build, so no compute figures apply. The 3.9 MB working set is the supplementary archive itself.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the Europe PMC supplement and list the files. It is one PDF of figures and zero data tables - five minutes, and it kills the candidate outright.

verdict_reason: Single-toxin mechanistic wet-lab study with no machine-readable data: the entire supplement is an 11-page PDF of gel photographs and AlphaFold3 confidence plots, verified by extraction. Fails Part A1 (no dataset deposited anywhere), A2 (no label column exists), A4 (no units, only gel images) and most decisively A5 (one toxin, one species, roughly one labelled observation against a ~1,500-row bar).
